chunks: Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Haytham narrated to us. He said: Abbad b. Ya'qub al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Anbasa b. Bijad al-Abid narrated to me. He said:

When Isma'il b. Ja'far b. Muhammad died and we finished his funeral, al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) sat down and we sat around him. He was silent and downcast. Then he raised his head and said: O people! This world is the abode of departure, and an abode of crookedness, not of straightness. However, the departure from the beloved brings a burning that cannot be repelled and a woe that cannot be deterred. People are only distinguished by beautiful mourning and soundness of thought. Whoever does not mourn for his brother, his brother will mourn for him. Whoever does not send forth a child, then he himself will be the one who proceeds without a child. Then he (peace be upon him) recited the words of Abu Khirash al-Hudhali mourning his brother: Do not think that I have forgotten his covenant, but rather my patience, O Umaym, is beautiful.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say at the funeral of his son Isma'il about mourning and patience?
ai.summary: Anbasa b. Bijad al-Abid narrates that when Isma'il, the son of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, died and the funeral was complete, the Imam sat down surrounded by his companions. After a period of silent grief, he raised his head and delivered a profound eulogy: This world is an abode of departure and crookedness. The burning pain of losing a beloved cannot be repelled nor can the grief be deterred. People are distinguished only by the beauty of their mourning and the soundness of their thinking. He concluded by reciting a line of poetry by the pre-Islamic poet Abu Khirash al-Hudhali, affirming that his outward patience does not mean forgetting. The original audience would have understood this as a masterclass in dignified grief — the Imam modeling how to grieve deeply while maintaining composure and beautiful patience.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Qaqqaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Isma`il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Haytham narrated to us. He said: `Abbad b. Ya`qub al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: `Anbasa b. Bijad al-`Abid narrated to me.

He said: When Isma`il b. Ja`far b. Muhammad died and we left his funeral, al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) sat down, and we sat down around him. He was melancholy. Then, he raised his head and said: O people! This world is the abode of departure – an abode of crookedness and not an abode of straightness. Departure is a tragedy that cannot be repelled and a woe that cannot be deterred. Surely, people are only distinguished by beautiful mourning and good contemplation. Whoever does not mourn for his brother, his brother will mourn for him. Whoever does not have a child, then he is the one who will proceed [toward death] without a child.  Then, he (as) presented the poem of Abi Khurash al-Hadhali when he mourned for his brother: “Do not think that I have forgotten his covenant, but rather, my patience – O Amim – is beautiful.”
